entries.title: An introduction to music theory: 7 Harmony: the triad
entries.section: Section 7, Example 63 and paragraphs on root, third, fifth and the order of major/minor thirds
entries.evidence: Triads stack two thirds. Major uses 4 then 3 semitones; minor uses 3 then 4. A triad in root position consists of root, third and fifth.
entries.application: Independent check of A-C-E, C-E-G and C-Eb-G, with octave/register checked against MIDI. Also supports the distinct qualities of C–E and D–F in the new melodic interval lessons; these two-note exercises are not triads. Batch 08: section 7, paragraph following Example 63, explicitly names E–G and D–F as minor thirds (3 semitones); checked in registers E4/G4 and D3/F3. Batch 09: C4–E4 has 4 semitones (major third); E3–G3 has 3 (minor third), as explicitly named following Example 63.
entries.limits: This source supports harmony, not the exact piano fingers, tempo or project exercise sequence. No historical performer attribution.

entries.section: Page marker 17, numbered point 3 (Gleichheit der Haltung); adjacent discussion of equal timing and note endings
entries.editionVerification: The edition and page-marker policy were checked on 2026-11-05 in batch 02; this batch read the separate authored letter-2 passage.
entries.evidence: In even scale-like playing, the earlier key is released at the entry of the next tone, maintaining continuity and even note lengths.
entries.application: Connection of adjacent different notes in both hands; contrast with previously prepared non-legato, then a three-note change of direction.
entries.limits: A historical discussion of even runs, not a prescription for every articulation. No adoption of rigid arm/wrist instructions elsewhere in the letter or compulsory half-hour drills. No facsimile check, no claim that Czerny composed these four patterns, specified their tempo, approved MIDI tolerances or taught a named performer these exact exercises.

entries.author: The Open University / OpenLearn
entries.title: An introduction to music theory: 6.4 Intervals
entries.section: Interval number paragraph and Example 60; distinction between harmonic and melodic intervals; minor-third paragraph with Example 61
entries.evidence: Interval number counts scale degrees inclusively. The same pitches may sound together or successively; the latter is a melodic interval. Minor thirds contain three semitones. Chapter 7 explicitly identifies C–E as major and D–F as minor.
entries.application: Play D4/F4 successively with RH 2/4 and C3/E3 with LH 5/3, omitting the intervening white key. Check the selected registers independently against MIDI 62/65 and 48/52. Batch 08: RH E4/G4 = 64/67 with 3/5 and LH D3/F3 = 50/53 with 4/2; intermediate F4/E3 are silent. Section 7 supplies the exact minor-third qualities.
entries.limits: Supports interval terminology and quality, not these exact fingers, project register choices, tempo 52, timing tolerances or exercise sequence. Does not prove independent aural recognition or teacher approval.

implementationApplications.section: Section 6.4, paragraphs surrounding Examples 60–61: C–E is a third; simultaneous notes form a harmonic interval; a minor third has three semitones.
implementationApplications.application: Our MIDI values independently give C4–E4/C3–E3 = 4 and D4–F4/D3–F3 = 3 semitones. These are dyads, not triads or a full scale.
implementationApplications.limits: Read the HTML text; no claim to have inspected Example 60 image/audio or a printed fingering.

entries.author: Chelsey Hamm and Bryn Hughes
entries.title: Open Music Theory: Intervals
entries.edition: Online edition, I. Fundamentals, chapter Intervals; no fixed publication date asserted
entries.section: Size; Perfect, Major, and Minor Qualities, Example 4; The Major Scale Method, steps 1–4; Augmented and Diminished Qualities, paragraph after Example 7
entries.evidence: Count written scale positions inclusively; distinguish melodic succession from harmonic simultaneity. The major-scale method yields perfect fourths/fifths within the tonic major scale; lowering a major third by a half step makes it minor.
entries.application: Independent classification of C4–Eb4, C4–F4 and C4–G4. MIDI checks 60/63, 60/65 and 60/67 confirm 3/5/7 semitones; these calculations are project validation, not the authors' recommended identification procedure.
entries.limits: The authors advise against counting half steps as the primary interval-identification method. This source does not establish these exact piano fingers, tempo, rhythm, physical comfort, aural-test validity or teacher approval. No score example was copied.

applications.application: Перейди правой с чёрной A♯4 безымянным 4 на белую B4 большим 1. Это полутон вверх: большой подходит к ближайшей белой, а A♯4 освобождается после нового звука. Знакомый переход B♭4–C5 через тон теперь сокращается до A♯4–B4 через полутон.

Свяжи A♯4–B4–C♯5 правой 4–1–2: после большого продолжи к чёрной указательным. Слышатся полутон, затем тон; среднюю B4 сыграй один раз. Соедини подготовленное подкладывание с новым продолжением без остановки.

applications.application: С белой B4 большим 1 перейди вниз на соседнюю чёрную A♯4 безымянным 4 через полутон. Сократи знакомый целый тон после большого, сохрани плавную передачу и свободную кисть.
Свяжи B4–A♯4–G♯4 правой 1–4–3: после большого сразу продолжи с безымянного на средний по двум чёрным. Общая A♯4 звучит один раз, без повторного нажатия или остановки.
С чёрной F♯5 указательным 2 перейди вниз на соседнюю белую E♯5 большим 1 через полутон. Сократи знакомый целый тон до соседней белой, сохрани плавную передачу и свободную кисть.
Свяжи F♯5–E♯5–D♯5 правой 2–1–3: после полутонового входа на большой продолжи средним на чёрную. Общая E♯5 звучит один раз, без повторного нажатия или остановки.
Соедини подготовленные 2–1–3 и 3–2–1 в F♯5–E♯5–D♯5–C♯5–B4: общая D♯5 средним 3 звучит один раз. Сохрани ровную передачу с большого на средний и продолжи к B4 без остановки в месте соединения.
Соедини подготовленные 1–4–3 и 3–2 в B4–A♯4–G♯4–F♯4: общая G♯4 средним 3 звучит один раз. После выхода с большого продолжи по чёрным к F♯4 без повторного нажатия общей ноты.
